title: GTFS Scorecard program report bundle plan
description: What /bundle/plan.json may say. This is the only document on the site that carries a price and a checkout link, and web/src/bundle.js renders the buy controls from it client-side, so nothing in the served HTML shows a malformed plan. Top level is closed (additionalProperties: false) so a new field cannot reach the page without a schema update, the same enforcement point as artifact.schema.json. The prices themselves are not pinned here: they are a hand-set hypothesis recorded in docs/program-plan.md and scripts/stripe-setup.sh, and their agreement across those three files is gated by pipeline/tests/test_bundle_plan_contract.py rather than by this contract.

paymentsAvailable.description: Whether the page may offer checkout at all. False renders every plan as "Not yet available"; true is a claim that each product below can actually be bought, which the conditional at the foot of this schema enforces.

currency.description: ISO 4217 alphabetic code, upper case. bundle.js hands it to Intl.NumberFormat, which throws on anything else and silently falls back to "<amount> <currency>".

provisioning_business_days.description: The refund-backed delivery promise the page prints. A zero or a negative would publish a promise nobody can keep.

products.description: Exactly the four knobs docs/program-plan.md names and scripts/stripe-setup.sh creates. Closed in both directions: a missing key is a plan the page cannot render, and an extra key is a product nothing on the Stripe side backs.

allOf.description: paymentsAvailable: true is a claim about every product, not about the page. bundle.js renders a buy control only where price is a number and checkout_url is truthy, so a null in either field ships a card reading "Not yet available" under a banner reading "Checkout is open" — an absence rendered as an offer. Either every product is sellable or the tier is off.

price.description: Whole units of the plan currency, not cents: bundle.js formats it with Intl.NumberFormat. Null means the product is not for sale, which paymentsAvailable: true forbids.

checkoutUrl.description: A Stripe Payment Link, or null when the product is not for sale. Restricted to buy.stripe.com because bundle.js accepts any https URL, so a typo'd or substituted host would render as a working buy button. Test-mode links (buy.stripe.com/test_...) are refused: the committed file is what the live page serves, and a test link there collects nothing.

oneTimeProduct.description: A one-off archive. interval must be null: bundle.js prints "per <interval>" whenever the field is truthy, so a stray value here advertises a subscription the Stripe price does not create.

monthlyProduct.description: Pinned to "month" rather than merely "a non-empty string": the interval is what the page bills the buyer, and swapping it for "year" on a monthly Stripe price prints $49 a year over a subscription that charges monthly.

everyProductSellable.description: Applied to products as a whole, with no properties of its own, so additionalProperties reaches all four keys rather than only unlisted ones.
